history.summary: TOWN REFINEMENT: the shrine is at Alorna in Pernem taluka, North Goa (not Pernem town proper). Vetal (Betala/Vetoba) is a Bhairava form of Shiva worshipped across Goa, the Konkan coast, Sindhudurg and Karwar as Kshetrapala/gramadevata — a guardian deity believed to protect the locality from calamities, witchcraft and snakebites. The deity is the patron of Maratha, Kalavant, Goud Saraswat, Rajapur Saraswat and Daivadnya communities. No founding date is documented for the Alorna shrine; it is an active devasthan with a public Instagram presence (@vetal_devastan_alorna). It is distinct from the well-known Shree Betal temple at Amona (Bicholim) and from the old Vetal temple at Harmal. Coordinates and the 7:00 AM–6:00 PM hours are from the temple's public place listing.

name: Shri Vetaleshwar Temple
town_description: Alorna is a village in Pernem taluka, North Goa, on the Chapora river. It is known for the historic Alorna (Halarn) fort overlooking the river, and lies in the temple-dotted hinterland east of Pernem town.
tradition: Shaivism — Vetal as Kshetrapala (guardian deity) and Bhairava form of Shiva

travel.airport: Manohar International Airport, Mopa (nearest, ~30 km); Dabolim Airport (~65 km)
travel.railway: Pernem railway station on the Konkan Railway (~10 km)
travel.road: By road from Pernem town via village roads; Pernem is on NH-66

visitor_information.opening_hours: 7:00 AM–6:00 PM daily (per the temple's public listing)
